question.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}4 & -1 & 2 \\ 4 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}],\,v=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3 \\ 0\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrix $A$ and vector $v$ shown above. Which of the following statements are true?

I. $v$ is an eigenvector corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda =2$ of $A$

II. $v$ is a generalized eigenvector of rank $2$ corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda =2$ of $A$

III. $v$ is a generalized eigenvector of rank $3$ corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda =2$ of $A$
question.worked_solution:
A *generalized eigenvector* ${v}_{n}$ of rank $n$ corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda $ of a matrix $A$ is a nonzero vector such that

$$
{v}_{n}\overset{A-\lambda I\,}{\to }{v}_{n-1}\overset{A-\lambda I\,}{\to }…\overset{A-\lambda I\,}{\to }{v}_{1}\overset{A-\lambda I\,}{\to }0,
$$

where ${v}_{n-1},{v}_{n-2},…,{v}_{1}\ne 0.$ An *eigenvector* is simply a generalized eigenvector of rank $1.$

First, we compute $A-2I:$

$$
A-2I=[\begin{aligned}4 & -1 & 2 \\ 4 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]-2[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 2 \\ 4 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}]
$$

- Next, we find the image of $v$ under the action of $A-2I:$

$$
(A-2I)v=[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 2 \\ 4 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3 \\ 0\end{aligned}]={{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{w}\ne 0
$$

- Since we got a nonzero vector in the last step, we now compute the image of $w$ under the action of $A-2I:$

$$
(A-2I)w=[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 2 \\ 4 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=0
$$

So, we obtain the following chain of maps:

$$
{{[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{v}\overset{A-2I\,}{\to }{{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{w}\overset{A-2I\,}{\to }{{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{0}
$$

Here, we see that $A-2I$ maps $v$ to $0$ in $2$ steps.

Therefore:

$\,$ *$v$ is a generalized eigenvector of rank $2$ corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda =2$ of $A.$*

So, the correct answer is "II only."
